newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Pasminco says plans lower Century cost.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Pasminco says plans lower Century cost.

text.p: Base metals miner Pasminco ltd said on Wednesday it hoped to cut by about 10 percent the A$1 billion development cost originally estimated for the Century Zinc deposit in north Queensland.
"We hope to get it down at least 10 percent," chief executive David Stewart.
He said the savings would be achieved by outsourcing some of the costs, including the mine fleet which would be supplied by contract miners.
Stewart said the company had initially adopted the original mine plan formulated by RTZ-CRA and were not combing through the plan to find cost savings.
"We are revisiting that to see if we can change some of the ways in which the mine was to be developed and operated with a view to saving some of the costs," Stewart told reporters.

In January, Pasminco said it would buy the Century Zinc and Dugald River zinc projects from RTZ-CRA for A$345 million conditional on the Queensland government issuing mining leases which depend on Century Zinc and Aborginal groups resolving a current impasse over land rights.
